text:
sam: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection PR landed yesterday we're seeing a 18-22% regression on multi-GPU throughput for autoregressive workloads when using KV sharding. p99 latencies are spiking and all-reduce time looks higher than before. :eyes:
anya: Ugh, thanks. Is this across TP and PP configs or just TP?
sam: Mostly when TP+PP are both present (hybrid runs). Single-mode DP runs look fine. Problem appears when KV cache is sharded across tensor-parallel ranks and we attempt to prefetch prefixes.
lee: I ran a quick perf trace. Attaching the key slices from the exec trace + a tiny CLI dump:
```
# run: ./runtest --model gptx-20b --pp 2 --tp 4 --kv-shard=per-tp --batch 8 --prefetch yes
tokens/sec: 2100  (expected ~2600)
all-reduce avg: 3.9ms -> used to be 2.1ms
kernel-switches/frame: 14
cpu->gpu memcpy spikes on step 0/1
```
jordan: Interesting — all-reduce almost doubled. Could be smaller tensor sizes hitting a less-optimized path after kernel selection heuristics changed. We swapped a small-matmul kernel to the generic cuBLAS path for sequences < 64 during the PR.
anya: That could blow up latency if it increases the number of collective calls or breaks overlap. Do we have timeline traces showing compute vs comm overlap?
perf-bot: perf summary: flamegraph: https://perf.internal/redwood/2176543210/flame.svg, timeline: https://perf.internal/redwood/2176543210/timeline.html (hit: increased sync gaps between KV prefetch and attention compute) :robot_face:
sam: Timeline shows a 1.8x gap where TP ranks wait on PP all-reduce completion before they can proceed with attention. Looks like prefetch order + kernel choice is preventing concurrent compute on some ranks.
lee: Repro steps: swap to `--kv-shard=per-pp` and tokens/sec returns to ~2550. So sharding across PP nodes seems to avoid the regression.
jordan: That suggests the issue is an interaction between tensor-parallel local shard layout and the new small-matmul kernel that serializes ops. In TP per-tp sharding we do more fine-grained all-reduces with smaller payloads — the new kernel might be forcing synchronous collectives.
anya: Quick mitigation options: 1) revert kernel micro-change for small mats 2) change batcher to coalesce tensors so all-reduce payloads are larger 3) alter KV prefetch ordering to favor PP-local fetch first. Which is lowest-risk?
sam: Revert is lowest-risk but blocks the perf win for other workloads. Coalescing in the batcher sounds promising — it keeps the new kernel but reduces collectives.
lee: I sketched a batching heuristic: when tp > 1 and kv-shard=per-tp, if seq_len < 64 then delay prefetches up to 8ms to aggregate into one larger all-reduce per step. Pseudocode:
```
if tp_count > 1 and kv_shard == 'per-tp' and seq_len < 64:
  prefetch_window_ms = min(8, latency_budget/2)
  aggregate_and_send()
else:
  send_immediately()
```
jordan: Delay is risky for latency-sensitive tails but better than 20% throughput loss. We can make it adaptive: start with 4ms and increase if we detect small collective inefficiency. Also add metric: all_reduce_bytes_per_call.
anya: Can we add a quick A/B in the infra? Canary the batching change on a dedicated cluster with synthetic load. I'll wire up a small eval harness.
perf-bot: queued job: kv-shard-batcher-sweep-2176543210 (canary cluster). Results expected ~2h.
sam: For the kernel path, I'll open an issue that links the flamegraph and request a revert patch if we see no fast fix from batching. For now, implement the adaptive coalescing as a short-lived mitigation. @jordan please own the patch, @anya please own canary. :thumbsup:
jordan: On it. I'll also add tracepoints for `all_reduce_start/all_reduce_end` and `kv_prefetch_enqueue/complete` so we can measure overlap precisely.
lee: FYI I tested DP-only and the coalesced approach gives small win too (3-5%) by reducing call overhead, so sounds like a net positive.
anya: Great. If adaptive coalesce lands, let's also add an opt-in env var `RW_KV_COALESCE_MS` for quick toggles.
sam: Sounds good. Thanks everyone — prioritize visibility in console (per-route all_reduce metrics) so SRE can alert if we accidentally flip it on cluster-wide.
perf-bot: note: linked debug artifact: /artifacts/kv-prefetch-exectrace-2176543210.tar.gz
lee: I'll paste a tiny snippet from the trace that shows the blocking pattern:
```
TP-rank0: kv_prefetch -> enqueue_ar -> wait(all_reduce) [3.7ms]
PP-rank0: compute(attn) -> needs_kv -> enqueue_ar -> early_finish [0.9ms]
```
jordan: Looks like imbalance — TP ranks are waiting on many small ARs while PP ranks finish earlier. Fixing aggregation should re-balance.
anya: Ok plan: jordan implement adaptive coalesce PR -> perf canary -> revert kernel if fails. I'll update the incident board.
sam: Filing followups: https://go/redwood/issue/INF-2389 (includes links to traces, perf job, and PR).
